decisions.reason: Changing the AXP2101 thermal-pad stencil aperture does not alter the required VBACKUP breakout, location, purpose, or population state.

The source reports normal VBUS connectivity and changes only the AXP2101 center-pad stencil pattern; it does not change high-current copper continuity, bottleneck, current-capacity, or stitching requirements.
The windowpane stencil decision does not change the PWROK pin breakout or its debugging purpose.
The source changes the paste aperture beneath the AXP2101 thermal pad, not the placement of AXP2101 or MT3608 decoupling capacitors.
The AXP2101 thermal-pad stencil change is unrelated to the retained ESP32 decoupling-capacitor placement.
The source retains the AXP2101 and changes only its assembly stencil treatment; it does not change the selected PMIC, power path, system rails, simultaneous charging behavior, or efficiency goal.
The stencil-aperture modification does not change battery overcharge, overdischarge, NTC, or thermal-protection requirements.
The source does not change the MT3608 rail, its GPIO control, enabled operating pattern, output rating, or sensor loads.
Changing the AXP2101 center-pad stencil pattern does not resolve or alter the intended VRTC connection.
The AXP2101 stencil modification does not change the panel power-button connector, PWRON signal connection, location, or switch behavior.
The thermal-pad stencil decision does not change the battery connector family, pin count, functions, accessibility, compatibility, or unresolved pin order.

Although the suspected solder defect affects DCDC1-side pins, the source changes only the stencil aperture and does not change DCDC1's required voltage, current rating, rail role, or compensation target.
